# Exponential Decay Schedules
Also called: Geometric LR Decay, Multiplicative LR Decay

## Overview
Exponential decay schedules reduce the learning rate multiplicatively over training steps, providing a smooth, continuous transition from high initial exploration to fine-grained convergence. This family differs from [Linear Learning Rate Schedule](11850-linear-learning-rate-schedule.md) by applying relative reductions rather than absolute ones, and from [Cosine Decay Learning Rate Schedule](14118-cosine-decay-learning-rate-schedule.md) by avoiding the symmetric "slow-fast-slow" trajectory in favor of a monotonic decrease . It is primarily used in [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) optimization to stabilize training when the model has converged to a coarse geometry but requires precise refinement of appearance and density fields.

## Shared principles
All methods in this family compute the learning rate $lr_t$ at step $t$ using a base raised to a power proportional to the normalized step count. The core mechanism is:
$$ lr_t = lr_{initial} \times \gamma^{\frac{t}{T}} $$
where $\gamma$ is the decay factor ($0 < \gamma < 1$) and $T$ is a normalization constant (often total steps or a specific interval). This ensures the learning rate never reaches zero but asymptotically approaches it. Unlike step decay, there are no discrete jumps. The schedule is often combined with warm-up phases to prevent early instability .

## Subtopics

### [Training Loop with Adaptive Regularization & LR Decay](2408-training-loop-with-adaptive-regularization-lr-decay.md)
Defines the standard iterative optimization protocol for NeRFs, combining ray-batched [SGD](#15522-sgd-street-view-synthesis-with-gaussian-splatting-and-diffus.md) with exponential LR decay and a two-phase loss schedule. It differs from [FreeNeRF](7471-pixelnerf.md) by using simpler auxiliary models for [depth supervision](#14220-depth-supervision.md) rather than annealing [positional encoding](#876-positional-encoding.md) frequencies, and explicitly manages regularization weights that decay alongside the learning rate.

### [Exponential Decay Learning Rate Schedule](9145-exponential-decay-learning-rate-schedule.md)
Applies a base raised to a normalized step exponent to transition from an initial to a final value. It differs from [Linear Learning Rate Schedule](11850-linear-learning-rate-schedule.md) by applying multiplicative reductions rather than additive ones, and from [Step Decay Learning Rate Schedule](11852-step-decay-learning-rate-schedule.md) by providing a continuous curve rather than discrete uniform reductions at specific boundaries.

### [Exponential Decay Learning Rate Schedule with Warm-up](14980-exponential-decay-learning-rate-schedule-with-warm-up.md)
Combines a linear warm-up phase with an exponential decay trajectory, specifically targeting per-camera exposure parameters or main network weights. It distinguishes itself from [Cosine Decay Learning Rate Schedule](14118-cosine-decay-learning-rate-schedule.md) by using a constant rate during warm-up followed by geometric decay, and from [Exponential Decay Learning Rate Schedule](9145-exponential-decay-learning-rate-schedule.md) by explicitly incorporating a delayed warm-up period to stabilize initial training.

## Background
Exponential decay is a standard technique in optimization, widely adopted in early neural network training and retained in NeRF pipelines for its simplicity and effectiveness in [fine-tuning](#9138-fine-tuning.md) . In the context of [differentiable volume rendering](#43-differentiable-volume-rendering.md), it addresses the problem of converging sparse input data by preventing large gradient updates once the model has established a coherent geometric prior .
